items.title: Malaysia has sufficient fuel supply despite Middle East tensions: Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has secured sufficient fuel supply until the end of the year despite ongoing disruptions caused by tensions in the Middle East, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said the government has secured alternative fuel sources as part of contingency measures to mitigate risks arising from prolonged instability in the region, including disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. He said the government was focused on balancing two priorities, namely ensuring a stable fuel supply while keeping fuel affordable for consumers.

items.title: Buntong tragedy: Families coping well after loss of two schoolgirls
items.summary: IPOH: The families of the two schoolgirls who died in the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats tragedy in Buntong are coping well and do not require counselling at this stage. State Women, Family, Social Welfare, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Committee chairman Datuk Salbiah Mohamed said officers from the Social Welfare Department had visited and met the families following the tragedy, and found them to be in a stable condition despite their loss. Salbiah said the state government would continue strengthening community awareness and welfare programmes to help prevent similar incidents.

items.title: Police reclassify toddler's death as murder, father to be charged
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU: Police have reclassified the death of an 18-month-old boy as murder after nearly three years of investigation, with the child's biological father identified as the main suspect. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged by a doctor at the Emergency Department of Hospital Sultan Ismail on Sept 13, 2023. He said the child was brought to the hospital, unconscious, by his 40-year-old father.

items.title: United Asiapac prices IPO at 35 sen ahead of Aug 19 debut
items.summary: The IPO comprises 139.22 million new shares, giving the company an estimated market capitalisation of RM192.5 million based on the IPO price. The company provides well intervention services to upstream oil and gas operators throughout the lifecycle of hydrocarbon wells. Managing director Ahmad Fadzuli Ali said the IPO would strengthen the company's operational capabilities as demand for well intervention services continued to grow.

items.title: Company’s RM19.5m donation to Bersatu was due to project award after Muhyiddin’s minutes, MD says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Construction company Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin said his firm had donated RM19.5 million to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in 2021 and 2022, as he viewed the RM605.2 million government project awarded to his younger brother’s company Sutracom Sdn Bhd as being due to then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s 2021 minutes. Shahradzi’s brother’s company Sutracom was eventually awarded the project in October 2022. Shahradzi’s company’s Mamfor’s RM19.5 million donation to Bersatu was done in stages, namely RM10.5 million and RM9 million before and after the project was awarded.

items.title: Johari: Next Negri government must help plantations with replanting
items.summary: JEMPOL: The next Negri Sembilan government must help oil palm plantations undergo replanting, says Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. Johari said observations along the route to Felda Palong 3 showed that many existing oil palm trees were old. "I was driving past earlier and saw many old oil palm trees.

items.title: Australia's sudden housing chill seeps into economy
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's housing market is suffering its worst slowdown since the pandemic as rising borrowing costs and a sharp reversal in tax breaks shake confidence in a normally reliable source of economic growth. With home prices in Sydney and Melbourne down nearly 5.0 per cent so far this year, the chill is evident in fewer people at open houses, tumbling auction clearance rates, a plunge in loan enquiries and a slump in property sales. The New South Wales government in June cut its stamp-duty forecasts by A$5.3 billion (US$3.7 billion) over the next four years.

items.title: Bachok Amanah Youth chief claims trial to posting false info on fuel prices
items.summary: SEPANG: Bachok Amanah Youth chief Abdullah Aqili Romeli pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to posting false information on petrol and diesel prices. The offence also carries an additional fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence continues after conviction. MCMC prosecuting officer Nur Nazhzilah Mohammad Hashim asked the court to set bail at RM10,000 with one surety and to impose additional conditions deemed appropriate.

items.title: Gobind: Malaysia's AI ambition needs whole-of-nation push
items.summary: He said the government established AI Malaysia as a platform to pool the expertise, resources and stakeholders required to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem. AI Malaysia is a new institution tasked with shaping national AI policy, establishing direction and driving effective implementation. He added that AI Malaysia will support two key policy frameworks: the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint 2030 (MD 2030) and the Malaysia AI Plan 2026-2030.

items.title: Rohingya refugees housed at KL police headquarters pending relocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An air of uncertainty hung over the 113 Rohingya refugees temporarily housed at the city police headquarters as they awaited further action after undergoing documentation and identity verification checks. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks conducted during the documentation process at the police headquarters found that all the refugees possessed valid UNHCR documents. "The group comprised one Iraqi man, one Somali woman, one Indonesian woman married to a Rohingya refugee, and 110 Rohingya refugees, including 57 adults and 53 children.

items.title: Negri polls: PH can retain state, win more seats, says Chow
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Pakatan Harapan can defend its seats in Negri Sembilan and capture additional constituencies, Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said today. Chow, who recently campaigned in the state, said voter sentiment varied across the areas he visited. "There were areas with good support and areas where we faced challenges in mobilising voters," he said after a visit to the MI Equipment facility in Bayan Lepas.

items.title: Teacher pleads not guilty to sexually assaulting three male pupils
items.summary: BESUT: A teacher pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to four charges of committing physical and non-physical sexual assault against three male pupils since last year. Under the first charge, the accused was alleged to have committed physical sexual assault against a 12-year-old boy at a school cooperative at around 4.30pm in April 2025. Under the third charge, Muhammad Izzuddin is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault against another child aged 14 at the same location at around 2.40pm last May.

items.title: UN chief Guterres sounds out Cyprus sides on prospects for peace talks
items.summary: NICOSIA: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres begins a fresh effort on Tuesday to coax Cyprus' rival sides back into peace talks after nearly a decade of deadlock. Failure would prolong a dispute that strains ties between Nato allies Greece and Turkiye and weighs on Ankara's relations with the European Union. Guterres, whose term expires at the end of 2026, is due to meet Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman separately on Tuesday.

items.title: Malaysia to unveil new housing policy with 2030 abandoned projects target
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The government will launch the third National Housing Policy 2026-2036 on Aug 10, introducing reforms aimed at improving housing affordability and eliminating abandoned housing projects nationwide by 2030. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the new policy is anchored on the principle of ensuring inclusive access to quality and affordable housing while addressing longstanding challenges in the sector. "The new National Housing Policy will introduce measures to make homes more affordable while addressing the long-standing issues of delayed and abandoned housing projects.

items.title: Malaysia has enough fuel supply until year-end, govt securing 2027 stocks, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Malaysia has begun securing fuel supplies for next year as the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz shows no signs of ending, with the government saying it has already ensured sufficient supply through the end of this year. He said Malaysia has managed to secure fuel supplies until the end of the year through mitigation measures and is now focused on ensuring supplies remain stable into next year. “We have managed to secure the fuel supply until year’s end, and we also have to try to secure supply for the coming year,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia must adopt AI while preserving values, says PM
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the country must ensure the adoption of the technology does not widen inequalities or erode its social values. This is a new challenge," he said at the launch of AI Malaysia Bhd here today. An AI nation means government and rakyat."

items.title: Mercedes-Benz writes off over 700 mn euros on China woes
items.summary: FRANKFURT: Premium German carmaker Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday reported falling profit at its car business as it wrote off over 700 million euros due to fierce competition in China. Though overall net profit for the quarter rose 13.5 per cent to 1.09 billion euros (US$1.24 billion), boosted by its vans and financial services businesses, core earnings at the key cars division fell 26 per cent to 909 million euros, Mercedes said, hit by competition in China. Including the write-down, profit at Mercedes-Benz's car business plummeted almost 94 per cent.

items.title: Taiwan detains Nvidia worker in chip smuggling probe
items.summary: TAIPEI: Prosecutors in Taiwan have detained an Nvidia employee as part of an investigation into the smuggling of the US tech giant's AI chips to China, a source familiar with the case told AFP on Tuesday. The man was detained after investigators raided his home and workplace on July 24, Keelung District Prosecutors Office said in a statement without mentioning Nvidia. Officials said in May they were investigating the shipment of "high-end" AI servers made by Nasdaq-listed Super Micro and containing advanced Nvidia chips to China, Macau and Hong Kong, in violation of US export controls.

items.title: Malaysia must raise wages before expanding tax base, says Akmal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia must address the structural issue of low wages before expanding its tax base through measures such as reintroducing a broad-based consumption tax, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. This follows the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD) recommendation that Malaysia consider reintroducing a broad-based consumption tax as part of wider tax reforms to strengthen government revenue. Akmal said income tax currently covers only about 15 per cent of Malaysia's workforce, highlighting the need to raise income levels before broadening the tax base.

items.title: France and Spain race to contain fires before new heatwave
items.summary: NAVALUENGA: Firefighters in France and Spain rushed to contain the worst wildfires in living memory Tuesday, seizing crucial hours before the arrival of another wave of searing temperatures. New heatwaves are expected to hit western Europe this week, with searing temperatures returning in France from Tuesday, and in Spain from Wednesday, meteorologists said. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the coming hours would be "absolutely decisive" to tame fires burning west of the capital, Madrid.

items.title: Khairy: BN still in the fight despite tougher Negri Sembilan contest
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Barisan Nasional (BN) still has a chance of winning and forming the Negri Sembilan government despite facing a tougher contest than in Johor, Khairy Jamaluddin said. The former Umno Youth chief said the remaining three days of campaigning would be crucial for BN candidates to reach as many voters as possible and outline their plans if elected. Despite the intense contest, he said BN remained optimistic of securing enough support to form the state government.

items.title: Police chief talks teen down from school building ledge
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Swift intervention by the Kuala Terengganu district police chief today prevented a 14-year-old girl from jumping off the second floor of a religious school building. Meanwhile, Kuala Terengganu Fire and Rescue station chief Thoyyibah Taib said the department received an emergency call at 9.33am. Firefighters found the student behaving aggressively while holding a knife on the second floor of the school building.

items.title: High Court orders Malaysian govt, police to pay activists RM195,000 over unlawful 2021 vigil arrests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The High Court today ordered the government and police to pay RM195,000 in damages to 13 activists after finding their arrests during a candlelight vigil for Covid-19 victims in 2021 were unlawful. Free Malaysia Today reported that Justice Datuk Anand Ponnudurai awarded each of the activists RM15,000 after holding the police officers involved and the government liable for the arrests made following the August 19, 2021 gathering at Dataran Merdeka. In his judgment, Anand said the activists were effectively deprived of their freedom after police seized their identity cards at the scene and directed them to go to the Dang Wangi police headquarters despite the gathering having ended.

items.title: KJ: I'll leave Keluar Sekejap if I return to politics full-time
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Khairy Jamaluddin says he will leave his Keluar Sekejap (KS) podcast if he returns to politics full-time, saying the platform must remain independent and not become a propaganda tool for any political party. The former Umno Youth chief said KS had built its reputation on balanced discourse and a willingness to criticise all sides, adding that maintaining that credibility would be difficult once he became politically affiliated. Khairy said he had asked KS co-founder Shahril Hamdan to hold him accountable if his views became overly aligned with any political party.

items.title: Foreigner held at KLIA after abusing staff over flight delay
items.summary: KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner Ravi Munusamy said the incident occurred about 7pm yesterday when the 25-year-old suspect became upset after the flight he was scheduled to board was delayed by five hours. "The man then hurled abusive remarks, issued threats and provoked airline staff on duty. Ravi said the suspect was subsequently arrested.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday with regional tech stock sell-off
items.summary: Among active stocks, VS Industry Bhd and SNS Network Technology Bhd slipped one sen each to 22 sen and 55 sen, respectively. Dagang NeXchange Bhd decreased two sen to 43 sen, while Tanco Holdings Bhd gained half a sen to 25 sen. Among the top gainers, Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd advanced 48 sen to RM91.78, Ideal Capital Bhd jumped 25 sen to RM4.00, Tenaga Nasional Bhd strengthened 20 sen to RM14.66, Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd added 18 sen to RM32.00, and KLCC Property Holdings Bhd increased 16 sen to RM8.85.

items.title: Myanmar approves death penalty for cyberscam offences
items.summary: YANGON: Myanmar's military-backed parliament approved a law on Tuesday that authorises capital punishment for those who detain or violently coerce victims into working in online scam centres, the speaker said. The "Anti-Online Scam Bill" was passed after MPs approved changes to a draft bill at a combined meeting of the lower and upper houses Tuesday morning in the capital Naypyidaw, Union Parliament Speaker Aung Lin Dwe said during a live television broadcast. Lower house MP Aye Chan confirmed to AFP that the death sentence remained in the approved version of the law.

items.title: Govt to strengthen AI safeguards against deepfakes, misinformation and scams
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: Putrajaya will continue strengthening measures to address threats from the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI), including deepfake technology, the spread of false information and online scams, as Malaysia develops its national AI ecosystem. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said while the government remained committed to expanding AI adoption among the public and industry, security and user trust could not be overlooked. He said awareness of the risks associated with AI misuse must be enhanced to ensure the technology was utilised responsibly.

items.title: Komtar tourist attraction cleared to continue operations after fatal fall, says Penang CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 28 — The operator of a tourist attraction in Komtar has been allowed to continue operating after the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) confirmed it had complied with all required safety measures following an incident involving an 18-year-old last weekend. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said JBPM had verified that the operator met all safety requirements and found no reason to halt operations. “The Fire and Rescue Department has confirmed that the operating company complied with all the required safety measures and has been allowed to continue operating,” he told reporters today after visiting a factory in Bayan Lepas.

items.title: HSS Engineers associate wins RM34mil water project contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HSS Engineers Bhd's associate SMHB Sdn Bhd has secured a RM34 million contract to provide consultancy services for the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS), including the sale of excess treated water to Penang. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, HSS Engineers said SMHB had accepted a letter of appointment from Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd for the Lead Design Consultancy and Detailed Design Consultancy 4 services package for the project. SMHB will provide lead design consultancy services for the NPWSS and detailed design consultancy for the project's water treatment plant.

items.title: Most infrastructure ready ahead of 2027 dual Year One intake, says education minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — The majority of infrastructure projects to support the intake of six-year-old Year One pupils for the 2027 school session have been completed ahead of schedule, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said. Fadhlina said the ministry is also making comprehensive preparations for teacher placement and other operational requirements based on projected student enrolment to ensure a smooth transition for the dual Year One intake. However, she noted that the ministry continues to receive inquiries and registration applications from parents even as planning for next year’s school session enters its final stage.

items.title: Govt still in talks over AI software for free youth access programme
items.summary: CYBERJAYA: Putrajaya is still in discussions with technology providers on the artificial intelligence (AI) software that will be offered under its free access programme to 100,000 Malaysian youths. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said details of the AI applications involved have yet to be finalised as negotiations were still ongoing. Gobind said the programme was part of the government's efforts to encourage AI awareness, access and adoption among Malaysians.

items.title: Perodua expands Sri Lanka export push with Traz, Alza models
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perodua has expanded its presence in Sri Lanka by exporting its latest model Traz, alongside its best-selling multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) Alza. Perodua president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Zainal Abidin Ahmad said Sri Lanka remains one of the company's largest export markets, with more than 20,000 units sold since 1997. Meanwhile, Alza is priced at 19.95 million Sri Lankan rupees (RM243,090).

items.title: Form Six transfer to Higher Education Ministry put on hold, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — The current pre-university management system for Form Six students will continue to be overseen by the Ministry of Education (MOE) for the time being, to ensure the smooth operation of the existing framework, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Elaborating further, the Prime Minister said that although Sixth Form remains under MOE, its students must have a distinct identity as post-secondary and pre-university learners. For example, Sixth Form students should not be included in general school assemblies.

items.title: MACC pursues documents from Dubai, Singapore and Indonesia as KWAP investment probe widens
items.summary: MELAKA, July 28 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has identified Dubai, Singapore and Indonesia as the three key jurisdictions from which it intends to obtain documents through the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process as part of its investigation into investment activities involving the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP). MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the commission is working with the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) to initiate the MLA process after determining that key documents related to the investments are believed to be located overseas. Since then, he said the MACC has recorded statements from 20 witnesses, including KWAP and MOF officials, members of KWAP’s Investment Committee, and investment panel members.

items.title: Komtar theme park met safety requirements, says Chow after student's fatal fall
items.summary: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the Fire and Rescue Department confirmed the operator's compliance following the incident . He said the theme park management also informed him that an internal memo was issued to all staff following the fall. "Following the incident, they issued a memo to all personnel to pay close attention to operations, crowd control and the management of visitors at the facility, and to remain vigilant," he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan DKU files fresh contempt bid against six over alleged injunction breach
items.summary: Free Malaysia Today reported that lawyer Steven Thiru, who represents the DKU and its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, said the application followed unsuccessful attempts to serve the six with documents from the earlier proceedings. Thiru alleged that the six had avoided service after the High Court granted his clients permission earlier this month to begin committal proceedings. High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain adjourned today’s committal hearing after lawyer Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud, representing the six, said the Court of Appeal would hear their application to stay the proceedings tomorrow.

items.title: Malaysia's PPI rises 9.2pct in June, highest in 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 9.2 per cent in June 2026, up from 7.8 per cent in the previous month, according to the Statistics Department. "The mining sector registered an increase of 29.0 per cent, following a 52.6 per cent rise in May 2026. The department said the agriculture, forestry and fishing sector increased 9.1 per cent, compared with 8.9 per cent in the previous month.

items.title: Police to question Kedah MB, Rembau Umno leader over N. Sembilan polls remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Police will call up Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and a Rembau Umno leader soon to record their statements over remarks made during the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police have so far received 11 reports against the Rembau Umno leader, while reports involving Muhammad Sanusi are still being updated, Berita Harian reported today. “Once police received two reports over statements issued by Datuk Seri Sanusi, investigation papers were opened under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: Malaysian govt prioritising wage growth before widening tax base, says economy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir today said Malaysia must first address its long-standing structural wage problem before considering any significant expansion of the country’s personal income tax base. Responding to the latest OECD Economic Survey of Malaysia, which recommended broadening the personal income tax base to increase government revenue, Akmal Nasrullah said the priority remains raising wages rather than taxing more Malaysians. Akmal Nasrullah said Malaysia’s tax challenges stem from a structural issue rather than simply a lack of tax instruments.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan early voter turnout passes 53pc as 18 centres close at noon
items.summary: Among the 18 centres that closed were Tent A, Jelebu District Police Headquarters (IPD) for the Chennah state seat; Tent B, Jelebu IPD (Pertang); Hall B, Dewan Serbaguna Jempol IPD (Jeram Padang); and Hall A, Dewan Emerald Nilai IPD (Lenggeng). Others included the Lecture Hall of Regiment 508 Kem Jalan Rasah (Nilai); Hall A, Dewan Serbaguna Kuala Pilah IPD (Seri Menanti); Hall C, Dewan Serbaguna Kuala Pilah IPD (Johol); and the Labu police station. Early voting involves 22,339 registered voters.

items.title: Penang monitoring Rohingya settlements after Penaga relocation, says chief minister
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 28 — The Penang government is monitoring areas with sizeable Rohingya communities following the voluntary relocation of 126 people from a temporary settlement in Penaga, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. Chow said the move was not a government enforcement operation, but had been initiated by the Rohingya community, with transport arranged for them to travel to Kuala Lumpur to seek assistance from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Police previously said the relocation last weekend was assisted and coordinated by the National Unity Department, the state government, the National Security Council, local community representatives and Rohingya representatives.

items.title: Kon Yeow: Mixed support means Pakatan must intensify Negeri Sembilan campaign in weaker seats
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 28 — Penang Pakatan Harapan chairman Chow Kon Yeow said PH needs to intensify its efforts in some Negeri Sembilan seats after seeing varying levels of support on the ground. He said the coalition will use the remaining days to consolidate its position in seats held before dissolution. The incumbent PH coalition is contesting all 36 seats.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan early voter turnout reaches 14.31pc as of 9am
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — As of 9am today, 14.31 per cent of early voters in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election have cast their ballots. A total of 38 polling centres opened simultaneously at 8am, allowing 22,389 registered early voters to fulfil their civic duty. For the latest updates, visit [https://prn.bernama.com/n9](https://prn.bernama.com/n9).

items.title: Anwar: Students to get free AI software access under digital skills programme
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today the government would subsidise subscriptions to top AI software to students under a newly-launched programme to raise artificial intelligence literacy. Anwar made the announcement as he launched AI Malaysia, a state-backed body tasked to accelerate AI adoption, align policies and drive AI-related innovation. Anwar also launched the National AI Technology Action Plan (2026–2030) booklet.

items.title: Bank Negara governor expects Malaysia’s growth to hit upper end of 4-5pc forecast despite energy shock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Despite the energy supply shock, Malaysia’s economy remains well on track to grow by four to five per cent, likely towards the upper end of the range, with manageable inflation in 2026, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. He said Malaysia’s economic fundamentals, reform agenda and commitment to sound economic management have enabled the government to respond when shocks occur. Abdul Rasheed said last year, Malaysia’s economy expanded 5.2 per cent, inflation remained contained and the ringgit was the region’s best-performing currency.

items.title: El Niño: Johor, Melaka could see 20-40pc less rain during upcoming Northeast Monsoon season
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Johor and Melaka are expected to record a reduction of between 20 to 40 per cent less rainfall when the country enters the Northeast Monsoon season at the end of this year due to the El Nino phenomenon, Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said. Mohd Hisham said the Northeast Monsoon typically begins in late October or early November and ends in late March, with the East Coast states usually receiving the highest rainfall in November and December. Meanwhile, Mohd Hisham said analysis of Malaysia's temperatures since the 1980s showed an increase of 0.19 degrees Celsius per decade due to global warming, while a strong El Niño could raise temperatures by up to 0.7 degrees Celsius above normal.

items.title: Anwar: Meritocracy must be fair to students with fewer opportunities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — Chasing meritocracy should not deprive students from marginalised groups of equal opportunities to succeed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Anwar said due consideration must also be given to students performing in rural schools despite lacking quality infrastructure or opportunities that their counterparts in urban schools enjoy. In April, the Education Ministry announced that all SPM students who scored 10As will automatically get a seat in matriculation programme.

items.title: Anwar: Learning other languages will not undermine Bahasa Melayu’s status
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said mastering other languages should not be seen as a pursuit that downgrades the significance of Bahasa Melayu as the national language. Anwar said ensuring all students master Bahasa Melayu as the language of knowledge remains his government’s priority but he said people must be more open and inclusive to learning other languages as well. Anwar said his administration has also pushed international schools to place a stronger emphasis on Bahasa Melayu and History, which was previously overlooked in some of these institutions.

items.title: OECD says Malaysia’s data centre boom brings growth but few jobs and mounting pressure on power, water
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Malaysia’s booming data centre industry is helping drive economic growth and foreign investment, but the OECD has warned that its rapid expansion is straining electricity and water supplies while creating relatively few jobs. In its latest Economic Survey of Malaysia report, the organisation said resilient economic growth has been supported by the global technology boom, with investment boosted by the rapid expansion of data centres, particularly in Johor. According to the OECD, Malaysia attracted approximately US$44 billion in data centre-related projects between 2021 and 2024, with total digital investments reaching US$65 billion during the same period.

items.title: OECD urges Malaysia to bring back GST, phase out fuel subsidies to strengthen public finances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has urged Malaysia to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) while gradually phasing out fuel subsidies, saying the measures are needed to strengthen the country’s finances as it edges closer to high-income status. In its latest Economic Survey of Malaysia released today, the Paris-based organisation said mounting spending needs for social protection, education and an ageing population would require a stronger and broader tax base. It recommended the government mobilise additional revenue by reintroducing the GST, broadening the personal income tax base and strengthening tax administration, while cushioning lower-income households through targeted cash transfers.

items.title: Seven-year-old boy recovering after surgery following Teluk Intan crash that killed two teen girls
items.summary: IPOH, July 28 — A seven-year-old boy who was involved in a crash that killed two teenage girls along Jalan Padang Tembak, Teluk Intan Sunday is in stable condition after undergoing surgery at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital here yesterday. Hilir Perak district police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the boy was at the shoulder of the road when a male driver, 28, lost control of his vehicle and skidded and crashed into the premises, owned by the boy’s father. — Bernama

items.title: Police open investigation after 11 reports over video allegedly touching on Negeri Sembilan royalty
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — Negeri Sembilan police have opened an investigation after receiving 11 reports over a TikTok video allegedly containing statements by a political party touching on the state's royal institution. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said investigators are examining the video's content and the context of the speech under Section 4(1) of the Election Offences Act 1954, Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. For the latest news on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Anwar: Form Six stays under Education Ministry, but schools must treat it as pre-university
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 28 — Form Six students will remain under the Education Ministry for now but schools should provide them with some special recognition, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. In March, Anwar had announced that Form Six students will be reclassified as post-secondary education and placed under the Higher Education Ministry’s purview. “School principals should handle Form Six students separately as a pre-university programme.

items.title: Early voting gets under way at Pusasda, Negeri Sembilan police headquarters
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 28 — A total of 1,481 military personnel and their spouses will cast their ballots today at the Army Basic Training Centre (Pusasda) in the early voting process for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election. Early voting is taking place under overcast skies. Meanwhile, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad visited the Negeri Sembilan police headquarters to observe the early voting process.

items.title: Fine weather expected for Negeri Sembilan early voting
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — The weather in almost all areas of Negeri Sembilan is expected to be favourable today morning as early voting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election takes place. In the afternoon, most areas across Negeri Sembilan are expected to experience heavy rain and thunderstorms. A total of 22,339 military and police personnel and their spouses will cast their ballots today in the early voting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election.

items.title: Small fire at KTM Mid Valley station caused by cloth falling on electrical wire
items.summary: The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said it received a report on the incident at 6.43pm, BuletinTV3 reported. It said seven firefighters from the Pantai Fire and Rescue Station, along with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) vehicle, were dispatched to the scene. Operations commander Senior Fire Officer I (PBK I) Zakaria Shaari said initial investigations found that the fire was believed to have started after a piece of cloth fell onto an electrical wire before catching fire and spreading to the roof insulation.

items.title: Tunku Abdul Rahman hopes F1 return delivers world-class experience for Malaysian fans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Tunku Panglima of Johor, Tunku Abdul Rahman Sultan Ibrahim, has expressed his hope that the organisers, including the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC), will deliver a world-class experience for race fans following the return of Formula 1 (F1) to Malaysia. Tunku Abdul Rahman, who is the President of Johor Motorsports Racing (JMR) and a racer himself, said the return of the prestigious event after a nine-year absence was a highly anticipated moment for the nation’s motorsports enthusiasts. The Tunku Panglima of Johor also shared his personal connection to the circuit, noting that the return of F1 would put Malaysia back on the global map in a positive light.

items.title: Petrol station price board near Sungai Besi damaged in fire, no casualties reported (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A sign displaying petrol prices at a petrol station along the North-South Expressway (NSE) heading towards Seremban near Sungai Besi caught fire last night. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.57pm before a team from the Seri Kembangan Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene, Berita Harian reported. He said the fire engine arrived at 10.06pm and found the blaze involved the price sign of a BHP petrol station.

items.title: Foreign man who accused cops of extortion is Interpol wanted over ‘scam’ case, says KL police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The foreign man who claimed he was extorted by individuals believed to be police officers has been identified as a person wanted in China in connection with a fraud case, police said. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the information was obtained through checks with the International Criminal Police Organisation (Interpol), Sinar Harian reported. Those detained included officers holding the ranks of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) and Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP), who were held to assist investigations.
